# TERM-0042 — Term cap for lower-income applicants

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **Status** | live since 2026-08-20 |
| **Module** | `policy_rules` · personal loans |
| **Owner** | Credit Policy · A. Naidoo |
| **Rule version** | 4 |
| **Shape version** | 1 *(unchanged since creation — only values have moved)* |
| **Implements** | Credit Policy §7.4.2 |
| **Acts on** | `term_cap` — reduces only, never raises |
| **Adjustable** | yes — the threshold and the cap may both be moved by an approved adjustment |
| **Reason code** | 2207 · "Term limited by affordability assessment" |

## What it does

> Where the applicant's monthly income is below the income floor, the maximum
> term is reduced to the lower-income cap. The reduction is a floor on risk: it
> can only shorten the term, never extend it.

## When it applies

| | |
|---|---|
| Products | personal loan (PL) |
| Segments | all |
| Effective | from 2026-08-20 00:00 SAST, no end date |
| Evaluated | on every application, before pricing |

> **This rule is currently modified by an adjustment.** ADJ-0117 "Q4 term
> competitiveness" raises the lower-income cap from 48 to 60 months for personal
> loans. It was approved on 2026-09-02 by M. Venter (Pricing) and expires on
> 2026-12-31 — **103 days remain**. Without it the cap would read 48 months. The
> rule's own definition still says 48 and has not been edited.
